speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, could you tell me exactly which antibiotic you were taking and how long before the fever, rash, and joint pain started? Also, have you noticed any swelling in your face, lips, or throat?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text: The distribution and timing strongly suggest serum sickness-like reaction, but I need to rule out other causes. Have you noticed any swelling of the hands, feet, or around the eyes, or any changes in urination? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of recurrent hematuria or proteinuria, and has anyone in your family had kidney disease? Also, does the rash blanch when you press on it? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Appearance Normal, WBC Within normal limits, RBC Within normal limits, Protein Negative, Glucose Negative

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal urinalysis and CBC, I am less concerned about IgA vasculitis or systemic infection. Do you have any joint swelling or redness, and have you developed any hives or angioedema? REQUEST TEST: C-Reactive_Protein

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal inflammatory markers and no evidence of organ involvement, the clinical picture of fever, pruritic rash, and arthralgia one week after starting amoxicillin is classic for a serum sickness-like reaction. DIAGNOSIS READY: Serum Sickness-Like Reaction
